title: What six common notebook mistakes really cost
request: Measure the cost of common notebook mistakes, wrong way against right way on identical data, so the copilot's severity and its 'show proof' rest on numbers rather than folklore.
spec: dclab_rnd/pitfalls.py and evidence/campaigns/pitfalls_v1: six experiments (preprocess before split, selection before CV, oversample before split, target encoding before split, random split on time data, holdout reuse for selection), each a question, a setup, facts, a recommendation and its limits.
plan: For each mistake, write the question and the wrong and right procedures before running.
Run on real datasets with several seeds; add a pure-noise canary where the mistake can fabricate signal.
Record the inflation as reported minus honest, with its limits.
Wire the results into the evidence index so the copilot cites them.

decisions.decision: Include a pure-noise canary (random labels, 2,000 features, 200 rows) for selection before CV.
decisions.why: On real tables with few features the inflation is tiny; the canary shows what the mistake does when candidates outnumber rows.

decisions.decision: Report harmless or reversed effects as measured.
decisions.why: The copilot's severity must follow the measurement; a scaler fitted before the split cost almost nothing, and a random split on HyperAck was not optimistic.

change: dclab_rnd/pitfalls.py (run, report) and six result files plus PITFALLS_REPORT.md under evidence/campaigns/pitfalls_v1/.

findings.defect: The assumption that a random split on time-stamped data is always optimistic did not hold.
findings.scenario: On HyperAck (11,107 orders over about four and a half months, 11 leakage-safe features, LightGBM) a random split reported ROC-AUC 0.9332 and training on the first 80% by time and testing on the last 20% gave 0.9371: the random split was 0.0038 lower, not higher.
findings.cause: The process was stable over that window, so a forward-in-time test scored as well or better.
findings.fix: The recommendation now says: validate forward in time when future rows will be scored, report that number, and measure the gap rather than assume its direction.

measurements.name: PIT-001 preprocess before split
measurements.gate: Logistic regression with mean imputation and scaling, 6 datasets, 3 seeds; inflation = fitted on all rows minus fitted on training rows.
measurements.next: Low severity for row-wise unsupervised transforms; still use a pipeline.

measurements.name: PIT-002 selection before CV
measurements.gate: SelectKBest plus logistic regression, 5-fold CV, 3 seeds, a noise canary and three real datasets.
measurements.result: Noise canary: 0.859 with selection before CV against 0.512 inside the folds (chance 0.5); real datasets at most +0.0041.
measurements.next: High severity for wide data (text, many engineered features).

measurements.name: PIT-003 oversample before split
measurements.gate: Random oversampling to 50/50, random forest, 4 imbalanced datasets, 3 seeds.
measurements.result: Up to +0.3003 ROC-AUC on average (online_shoppers 0.9019 reported vs 0.6016 honest).
measurements.next: Resample only inside training data and score on naturally imbalanced rows.

measurements.name: PIT-004 target encoding before split
measurements.gate: Mean-target encoding of one categorical column, histogram boosting, 80/20 split, 3 seeds.
measurements.result: Encoding Telco customerID (unique per row): 1.0000 vs 0.8160 honest (+0.1840); a low-cardinality HyperAck category: +0.0019.

measurements.name: PIT-005 random split on time data
measurements.gate: HyperAck orders, LightGBM on 11 leakage-safe features; random stratified 80/20 over 3 seeds against training on the first 80% by time.
measurements.result: Random 0.9332 vs time-ordered 0.9371 (random minus time -0.0038): not optimistic on this window.
measurements.next: Validate forward in time anyway when future rows will be scored, and report that number.

measurements.name: PIT-006 holdout reuse for selection
measurements.gate: 30 random LightGBM configurations, 60/20/20 split into training and two holdouts, 5 datasets, 3 seeds; bias = the pick's drop to the untouched holdout minus the average drop.
measurements.result: +0.0072 ROC-AUC optimism on average, +0.0177 on german_credit; on the untouched holdout the pick ranked 7.2 of 30 on average.
measurements.next: Tune on training CV and read the holdout once; the bias grows with the number of configurations.

outcome: Six measured precedents the copilot cites as proof: the large ones (oversampling up to +0.30, identifier encoding +0.18, selection on wide noise +0.35) and the small or reversed ones (scaling 0.0001, random vs time -0.0038).
lessons: The same mistake (fitting on all rows) ranges from harmless to fatal depending on what is fitted; severity must be measured per step.
Do not assume the direction of a validation gap; measure it.
